sanskrit: yathā sthalaṃ ca nimnaṃ ca na syād varṣati vāsave tathāsīt pṛthivī sarvā śoṇitena pariplutā
english: As when Vāsava pours down rain no place stays high or low, so was the whole earth then made level, flooded over with blood.

sanskrit: ṣaṭsahasrān varān vīrān punar daśaśatān varān prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among warriors dispatched to the realm of death six thousand chosen heroes and yet another thousand choice warriors, all of them kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ sahasraśo viddhā vidhivat kalpitā dvipāḥ śerate bhūmim āsādya śailā vajrahatā iva
english: Elephants pierced by arrows in their thousands, caparisoned in due order, sank to the ground and lay there like mountains struck down by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa vājirathamātaṅgān nighnan vyacarad arjunaḥ prabhinna iva mātaṅgo mṛdnan naḍavanaṃ yathā
english: Slaying horses, chariots, and elephants, Arjuna ranged across the field like a rutting elephant trampling down a thicket of reeds.

sanskrit: bhūridrumalatāgulmaṃ śuṣkendhanatṛṇolapam nirdahed analo 'raṇyaṃ yathā vāyusamīritaḥ
english: As fire fanned by the wind burns down a forest dense with trees, creepers, and thickets, heaped with dry fuel, grass, and brushwood,

sanskrit: sainyāraṇyaṃ tava tathā kṛṣṇānilasamīritaḥ śarārcir adahat kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavāgnir dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: so did Dhanaṃjaya, the Pāṇḍava-fire, fanned by the wind that was Kṛṣṇa, with arrows for his flames, burn down in fury the forest of your army.

sanskrit: śūnyān kurvan rathopasthān mānavaiḥ saṃstaran mahīm prānṛtyad iva saṃbādhe cāpahasto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Emptying the chariot-seats and strewing the earth with men, Dhanaṃjaya, bow in hand, seemed almost to dance amid the press.

sanskrit: vajrakalpaiḥ śarair bhūmiṃ kurvann uttaraśoṇitām prāviśad bhāratīṃ senāṃ saṃkruddho vai dhanaṃjayaḥ taṃ śrutāyus tathāmbaṣṭho vrajamānaṃ nyavārayat
english: Making the earth flow over with blood by his thunderbolt-like shafts, the enraged Dhanaṃjaya plunged into the Bhārata host; but Śrutāyus and the Ambaṣṭha chief checked him as he advanced.

sanskrit: tasyārjunaḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kaṅkapatraparicchadaiḥ nyapātayad dhayāñ śīghraṃ yatamānasya māriṣa dhanuś cāsyāparaiś chittvā śaraiḥ pārtho vicakrame
english: With sharp shafts fledged with heron feathers, O honored one, Arjuna swiftly brought down the horses of that struggling foe; and Pārtha, having sheared his bow apart with other arrows, pressed onward.

sanskrit: ambaṣṭhas tu gadāṃ gṛhya krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ āsasāda raṇe pārthaṃ keśavaṃ ca mahāratham
english: But the Ambaṣṭha chief, seizing his mace, his eyes clouded with wrath, fell upon Pārtha in battle and upon Keśava, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prahasan vīro gadām udyamya bhārata ratham āvārya gadayā keśavaṃ samatāḍayat
english: Then that hero, laughing aloud, O Bhārata, raised his mace and, blocking the chariot, smote Keśava with it.

sanskrit: gadayā tāḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā keśavaṃ paravīrahā arjuno bhṛśasaṃkruddhaḥ so 'mbaṣṭhaṃ prati bhārata
english: Seeing Keśava struck by the mace, Arjuna, slayer of hostile heroes, blazed into utter fury against the Ambaṣṭha chief, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarair hemapuṅkhaiḥ sagadaṃ rathināṃ varam chādayām āsa samare meghaḥ sūryam ivoditam
english: Then with golden-shafted arrows he covered that best of chariot-warriors, mace and all, even as a cloud veils the risen sun in battle.

sanskrit: tato 'paraiḥ śaraiś cāpi gadāṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ acūrṇayat tadā pārthas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then with still other arrows Pārtha smashed to powder the mace of that great-souled warrior; and the deed seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhyānyāṃ mahatīṃ gadām arjunaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca punaḥ punar atāḍayat
english: Then, seeing that mace fallen, he caught up another mighty mace and struck again and again at Arjuna and Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tasyārjunaḥ kṣuraprābhyāṃ sagadāv udyatau bhujau cicchedendradhvajākārau śiraś cānyena patriṇā
english: With two razor-edged arrows Arjuna severed both his upraised arms—shaped like Indra's banner—that still held the mace, and with a third feathered shaft his head.

sanskrit: sa papāta hato rājan vasudhām anunādayan indradhvaja ivotsṛṣṭo yantranirmuktabandhanaḥ
english: Slain, he fell, O king, making the earth resound, like Indra's banner-pole let go when the fastenings of its mechanism are loosed.

sanskrit: rathānīkāvagāḍhaś ca vāraṇāśvaśatair vṛtaḥ so 'dṛśyata tadā pārtho ghanaiḥ sūrya ivāvṛtaḥ
english: Plunged deep within the chariot-ranks and ringed by hundreds of elephants and horses, Pārtha then appeared like the sun shrouded by clouds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ praviṣṭe kaunteye sindhurājajighāṃsayā droṇānīkaṃ vinirbhidya bhojānīkaṃ ca dustaram
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when the son of Kuntī had broken through Droṇa's division and the well-nigh impassable division of the Bhojas, bent on slaying the king of the Sindhus,

sanskrit: kāmbojasya ca dāyāde hate rājan sudakṣiṇe śrutāyudhe ca vikrānte nihate savyasācinā
english: and when, O king, Sudakṣiṇa, heir of the Kāmboja, had been slain, and the valiant Śrutāyudha laid low by Savyasācin,

sanskrit: vipradruteṣv anīkeṣu vidhvasteṣu samantataḥ prabhagnaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā putras te droṇam abhyayāt
english: with the troops fleeing apart and shattered on every side, your son, seeing his own host broken, went up to Droṇa.

sanskrit: tvarann ekarathenaiva sametya droṇam abravīt gataḥ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ pramathyemāṃ mahācamūm
english: Hastening up on a single chariot, he came to Droṇa and said: "That tiger among men has passed through, after crushing this great army of ours."

sanskrit: atra buddhyā samīkṣasva kiṃ nu kāryam anantaram arjunasya vighātāya dāruṇe 'smiñ janakṣaye
english: "Consider now with your wisdom what must next be done to thwart Arjuna in this dreadful slaughter of men."

sanskrit: yathā sa puruṣavyāghro na hanyeta jayadrathaḥ tathā vidhatsva bhadraṃ te tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: "Contrive it so that Jayadratha, that tiger among men, be not slain—blessings upon you—for you are our highest refuge."

sanskrit: asau dhanaṃjayāgnir hi kopamārutacoditaḥ senākakṣaṃ dahati me vahniḥ kakṣam ivotthitaḥ
english: "Yonder Dhanaṃjaya-fire, driven by the wind of his wrath, burns the dry brush of my army, like a blaze risen amid the thicket."

sanskrit: atikrānte hi kaunteye bhittvā sainyaṃ paraṃtapa jayadrathasya goptāraḥ saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ
english: "For now that the son of Kuntī has burst through the army and passed beyond, O scorcher of foes, the guardians of Jayadratha have fallen into the gravest doubt."

sanskrit: sthirā buddhir narendrāṇām āsīd brahmavidāṃ vara nātikramiṣyati droṇaṃ jātu jīvan dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "Firm had been the conviction of the lords of men, O best of the knowers of Brahman, that Dhanaṃjaya could never while living pass beyond Droṇa."

sanskrit: so 'sau pārtho vyatikrānto miṣatas te mahādyute sarvaṃ hy adyāturaṃ manye naitad asti balaṃ mama
english: "Yet that Pārtha has passed through before your very eyes, O resplendent one; all this host I now reckon stricken—it is no longer an army of mine."

sanskrit: jānāmi tvāṃ mahābhāga pāṇḍavānāṃ hite ratam tathā muhyāmi ca brahman kāryavattāṃ vicintayan
english: "I know you, O greatly blessed one, to be devoted to the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas; and so I am bewildered, O Brahman, when I ponder what is to be done."

sanskrit: yathāśakti ca te brahman vartaye vṛttim uttamām prīṇāmi ca yathāśakti tac ca tvaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: "To the best of my power, O Brahman, I provide for your every want and please you as I am able; yet this you do not heed."

sanskrit: asmān na tvaṃ sadā bhaktān icchasy amitavikrama pāṇḍavān satataṃ prīṇāsy asmākaṃ vipriye ratān
english: "Though we are ever devoted to you, O you of measureless prowess, you do not wish us well; you forever favor the Pāṇḍavas, who delight in our undoing."

sanskrit: asmān evopajīvaṃs tvam asmākaṃ vipriye rataḥ na hy ahaṃ tvāṃ vijānāmi madhudigdham iva kṣuram
english: "Living off us, you yet take pleasure in what harms us; I had not understood you to be like a razor smeared with honey."

sanskrit: nādāsyac ced varaṃ mahyaṃ bhavān pāṇḍavanigrahe nāvārayiṣyaṃ gacchantam ahaṃ sindhupatiṃ gṛhān
english: "Had you not granted me a boon for the curbing of the Pāṇḍavas, I would never have stopped the lord of the Sindhus when he was going home."

sanskrit: mayā tv āśaṃsamānena tvattas trāṇam abuddhinā āśvāsitaḥ sindhupatir mohād dattaś ca mṛtyave
english: "But I, in my folly, hoping for protection from you, reassured the lord of the Sindhus, and so, deluded, have delivered him over to death."

sanskrit: yamadaṃṣṭrāntaraṃ prāpto mucyetāpi hi mānavaḥ nārjunasya vaśaṃ prāpto mucyetājau jayadrathaḥ
english: "A man caught between the fangs of Yama might yet escape; but Jayadratha, fallen into Arjuna's power, will never escape from the battle."

sanskrit: sa tathā kuru śoṇāśva yathā rakṣyeta saindhavaḥ mama cārtapralāpānāṃ mā krudhaḥ pāhi saindhavam
english: "So act, O you of the red steeds, that the Saindhava be saved; and be not angered at the laments of one in anguish—save the Saindhava."

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca nābhyasūyāmi te vācam aśvatthāmnāsi me samaḥ satyaṃ tu te pravakṣyāmi taj juṣasva viśāṃ pate
english: Droṇa said: I take no offense at your words; to me you are as Aśvatthāman. But I shall tell you the truth—accept it, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sārathiḥ pravaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śīghrāś cāsya hayottamāḥ alpaṃ ca vivaraṃ kṛtvā tūrṇaṃ yāti dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa is a peerless charioteer, and his fine horses are swift; making but a small opening, Dhanaṃjaya passes through in an instant.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu paśyasi bāṇaughān krośamātre kirīṭinaḥ paścād rathasya patitān kṣiptāñ śīghraṃ hi gacchataḥ
english: Do you not see the floods of Kirīṭin's arrows, loosed as he speeds swiftly on, falling fully a krośa behind his chariot?

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ śīghrayāne 'dya samartho vayasānvitaḥ senāmukhe ca pārthānām etad balam upasthitam
english: And I, weighed down with years, am no longer fit for swift pursuit today; moreover, this force of the Pārthas stands here at the army's front.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraś ca me grāhyo miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām evaṃ mayā pratijñātaṃ kṣatramadhye mahābhuja
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira is to be seized by me before the eyes of all the bowmen—thus have I vowed amid the kṣatriyas, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayena cotsṛṣṭo vartate pramukhe mama tasmād vyūhamukhaṃ hitvā nāhaṃ yāsyāmi phalgunam
english: Left behind by Dhanaṃjaya, he now stands before me; therefore I will not abandon the front of the array to go after Phalguna.

sanskrit: tulyābhijanakarmāṇaṃ śatrum ekaṃ sahāyavān gatvā yodhaya mā bhais tvaṃ tvaṃ hy asya jagataḥ patiḥ
english: Go yourself, with comrades at your side, and fight that single foe, your equal in birth and in deeds; have no fear—you are the lord of this world.

sanskrit: rājā śūraḥ kṛtī dakṣo vairam utpādya pāṇḍavaiḥ vīra svayaṃ prayāhy āśu yatra yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: You are a king, brave, accomplished, and skilled, and have stirred up enmity with the Pāṇḍavas; go yourself, O hero, swiftly to where Dhanaṃjaya has gone.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca kathaṃ tvām apy atikrāntaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ dhanaṃjayo mayā śakya ācārya pratibādhitum
english: Duryodhana said: When Dhanaṃjaya, the best of all who bear arms, has passed even beyond you, how, O teacher, am I able to hold him off?

sanskrit: api śakyo raṇe jetuṃ vajrahastaḥ puraṃdaraḥ nārjunaḥ samare śakyo jetuṃ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Puraṃdara, the thunderbolt-wielder himself, might be conquered in battle, but Arjuna, conqueror of hostile cities, cannot be conquered in war.

sanskrit: yena bhojaś ca hārdikyo bhavāṃś ca tridaśopamaḥ astrapratāpena jitau śrutāyuś ca nibarhitaḥ
english: He by whose blaze of weapons the Bhoja, the son of Hṛdika, and you yourself—a peer of the gods—were vanquished, and Śrutāyus struck down;

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇaś ca nihataḥ sa ca rājā śrutāyudhaḥ śrutāyuś cācyutāyuś ca mlecchāś ca śataśo hatāḥ
english: by whom Sudakṣiṇa was slain, and King Śrutāyudha, and Śrutāyus and Acyutāyus, and the mlecchas slain in their hundreds—

sanskrit: taṃ kathaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe dahantam ahitān bahūn pratiyotsyāmi durdharṣaṃ tan me śaṃsāstrakovida
english: how shall I fight against that unassailable Pāṇḍava in battle, who consumes so many of his foes? Tell me this, O master of weapons.

sanskrit: kṣamaṃ cen manyase yuddhaṃ mama tenādya śādhi mām paravān asmi bhavati preṣyakṛd rakṣa me yaśaḥ
english: If you deem battle with him fitting for me today, then direct me; I am at your bidding, your servant—guard my honor.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca satyaṃ vadasi kauravya durādharṣo dhanaṃjayaḥ ahaṃ tu tat kariṣyāmi yathainaṃ prasahiṣyasi
english: Droṇa said: You speak truly, O Kaurava—Dhanaṃjaya is hard to assail. Yet I shall so contrive it that you will be able to withstand him.

sanskrit: adbhutaṃ cādya paśyantu loke sarvadhanurdharāḥ viṣaktaṃ tvayi kaunteyaṃ vāsudevasya paśyataḥ
english: Let all the bowmen in the world behold today a marvel: the son of Kuntī held fast in combat with you, while Vāsudeva looks on.

sanskrit: eṣa te kavacaṃ rājaṃs tathā badhnāmi kāñcanam yathā na bāṇā nāstrāṇi viṣahiṣyanti te raṇe
english: Behold, O king, I bind upon you a golden corselet, so fashioned that neither arrows nor missiles shall prevail against you in battle.

sanskrit: yadi tvāṃ sāsurasurāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ yodhayanti trayo lokāḥ sanarā nāsti te bhayam
english: Though the gods with the asuras, with the yakṣas, serpents, and rākṣasas, and the three worlds together with men should war against you, you have nothing to fear.

sanskrit: na kṛṣṇo na ca kaunteyo na cānyaḥ śastrabhṛd raṇe śarān arpayituṃ kaś cit kavace tava śakṣyati
english: Neither Kṛṣṇa, nor the son of Kuntī, nor any other bearer of arms in battle shall be able to lodge his shafts in this corselet of yours.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ kavacam āsthāya kruddham adya raṇe 'rjunam tvaramāṇaḥ svayaṃ yāhi na cāsau tvāṃ sahiṣyate
english: So, donning this corselet, go yourself in haste this day against the wrathful Arjuna in battle, and he shall not withstand you.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā tvaran droṇaḥ spṛṣṭvāmbho varma bhāsvaram ābabandhādbhutatamaṃ japan mantraṃ yathāvidhi
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus, Droṇa, in haste, touched water and bound on that most wondrous, gleaming corselet, murmuring the sacred formula in due form.

sanskrit: raṇe tasmin sumahati vijayāya sutasya te visismāpayiṣur lokaṃ vidyayā brahmavittamaḥ
english: In that vast battle, for your son's victory, that foremost knower of Brahman, wishing to astonish the world with his lore, did so.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca karotu svasti te brahmā svasti cāpi dvijātayaḥ sarīsṛpāś ca ye śreṣṭhās tebhyas te svasti bhārata
english: Droṇa said: May Brahmā grant you well-being, and the twice-born grant you well-being; and from those that are foremost among creeping things, well-being to you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yayātir nahuṣaś caiva dhundhumāro bhagīrathaḥ tubhyaṃ rājarṣayaḥ sarve svasti kurvantu sarvaśaḥ
english: May Yayāti and Nahuṣa, Dhundhumāra and Bhagīratha, and all the royal sages in every way work your well-being.

sanskrit: svasti te 'stv ekapādebhyo bahupādebhya eva ca svasty astv apādakebhyaś ca nityaṃ tava mahāraṇe
english: Well-being be yours from the one-footed and from the many-footed alike, and well-being from the footless ones, ever, in the great battle.

sanskrit: svāhā svadhā śacī caiva svasti kurvantu te sadā lakṣmīr arundhatī caiva kurutāṃ svasti te 'nagha
english: May Svāhā, Svadhā, and Śacī ever work your well-being; may Lakṣmī and Arundhatī make for your well-being, O sinless one.

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva viśvāmitras tathāṅgirāḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapaś caiva svasti kurvantu te nṛpa
english: May Asita and Devala, Viśvāmitra and Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa work your well-being, O king.

sanskrit: dhātā vidhātā lokeśo diśaś ca sadigīśvarāḥ svasti te 'dya prayacchantu kārttikeyaś ca ṣaṇmukhaḥ
english: May Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, the Lord of the world, and the quarters with their guardians grant you well-being this day, and six-faced Kārttikeya as well.

sanskrit: vivasvān bhagavān svasti karotu tava sarvaśaḥ diggajāś caiva catvāraḥ kṣitiḥ khaṃ gaganaṃ grahāḥ
english: May the blessed Vivasvān work your well-being in every way, and the four elephants of the quarters, the earth, the sky, the firmament, and the planets.

sanskrit: adhastād dharaṇīṃ yo 'sau sadā dhārayate nṛpa sa śeṣaḥ pannagaśreṣṭhaḥ svasti tubhyaṃ prayacchatu
english: And he who from below forever upholds the earth, O king—that Śeṣa, foremost of serpents—may he grant you well-being.

sanskrit: gāndhāre yudhi vikramya nirjitāḥ surasattamāḥ purā vṛtreṇa daityena bhinnadehāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: O prince of Gāndhāra, of old the noblest of the gods, advancing in battle, were vanquished by the daitya Vṛtra, their bodies torn open in their thousands.

sanskrit: hṛtatejobalāḥ sarve tadā sendrā divaukasaḥ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmur vṛtrād bhītā mahāsurāt
english: All the dwellers of heaven then, robbed of their splendor and strength, with Indra at their head, took refuge in Brahmā, in terror of Vṛtra, that great asura.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ pramarditānāṃ vṛtreṇa devānāṃ devasattama gatir bhava suraśreṣṭha trāhi no mahato bhayāt
english: The gods said: To the gods crushed by Vṛtra, O noblest of deities, be a refuge, O best of the gods; save us from this great peril.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca atha pārśve sthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ śakrādīṃś ca surottamān prāha tathyam idaṃ vākyaṃ viṣaṇṇān surasattamān
english: Droṇa said: Then to Viṣṇu, who stood at his side, and to Śakra and the other foremost gods—those noblest deities, downcast—Brahmā spoke this true word.

sanskrit: rakṣyā me satataṃ devāḥ sahendrāḥ sadvijātayaḥ tvaṣṭuḥ sudurdharaṃ tejo yena vṛtro vinirmitaḥ
english: "The gods, with Indra and the twice-born, are ever to be protected by me. Most hard to withstand is the energy of Tvaṣṭṛ, by which Vṛtra was fashioned."

sanskrit: tvaṣṭrā purā tapas taptvā varṣāyutaśataṃ tadā vṛtro vinirmito devāḥ prāpyānujñāṃ maheśvarāt
english: "By Tvaṣṭṛ of old, after he had practiced austerity for a hundred times ten thousand years and gained the leave of Maheśvara, was Vṛtra fashioned, O gods."

sanskrit: sa tasyaiva prasādād vai hanyād eva ripur balī nāgatvā śaṃkarasthānaṃ bhagavān dṛśyate haraḥ
english: "That mighty foe can be slain only by His grace; yet the blessed Hara cannot be beheld without going to Śaṃkara's abode."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā haniṣyatha ripuṃ kṣipraṃ gacchata mandaram yatrāste tapasāṃ yonir dakṣayajñavināśanaḥ pinākī sarvabhūteśo bhaganetranipātanaḥ
english: "Having beheld Him, you shall slay the foe; go quickly to Mandara, where dwells the source of all austerities, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, the bearer of the Pināka, lord of all beings, who struck down Bhaga's eye."

sanskrit: te gatvā sahitā devā brahmaṇā saha mandaram apaśyaṃs tejasāṃ rāśiṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham
english: The gods, going together with Brahmā to Mandara, beheld a mass of radiance bright as ten million suns.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt svāgataṃ devā brūta kiṃ karavāṇy aham amoghaṃ darśanaṃ mahyaṃ kāmaprāptir ato 'stu vaḥ
english: He said: "Welcome, O gods; tell me what I am to do. The sight of me is never in vain; let your desire be fulfilled thereby."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te sarve pratyūcus taṃ divaukasaḥ tejo hṛtaṃ no vṛtreṇa gatir bhava divaukasām
english: Thus addressed, all those dwellers of heaven answered Him: "Our splendor has been carried off by Vṛtra; be the refuge of the dwellers of heaven."

sanskrit: mūrtīr īkṣaṣva no deva prahārair jarjarīkṛtāḥ śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapannāḥ sma gatir bhava maheśvara
english: "Behold our bodies, O god, battered to pieces by his blows; we have come to you for refuge—be our recourse, O Maheśvara."

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca viditaṃ me yathā devāḥ kṛtyeyaṃ sumahābalā tvaṣṭus tejobhavā ghorā durnivāryākṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Maheśvara said: I know, O gods, how this conjured being, of vast might and terrible, sprung from the energy of Tvaṣṭṛ, is hard for the unperfected of soul to ward off.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā kāryaṃ sāhyaṃ sarvadivaukasām mamedaṃ gātrajaṃ śakra kavacaṃ gṛhya bhāsvaram badhānānena mantreṇa mānasena sureśvara
english: But surely I must render aid to all the dwellers of heaven. Take, O Śakra, this gleaming corselet born of my own body, and bind it on, O lord of the gods, with this mind-born formula.
